answer: A concrete defense is interaction-graph diversity scoring: an agent's trust is measured by how varied its counterparties are, like light through a prism scattering into many distinct colors instead of one narrow beam. Sybil clusters are easy to spot because fake identities mostly trade with each other and a few controllers, leaving an umber-dark, tightly knotted subgraph, while honest agents weave a velvet-smooth web of many independent partners. Agents whose graph stays narrow pay higher fees and earn lower rewards until their connections genuinely diversify.
